resolution: Root-caused the 240->4fps cliff with the heartbeat probe (DOMINANT=gpu ~277ms/frame, present ~30us -> CPU-bound inside gpu.frame, not GPU fill, not paint/tick/GC). The cost is getOrCreateTexBindGroup in framework/gpu/3d.zig: its content-hash cache key was recomputed by hashTex walking the ENTIRE atlas every call, every frame, per textured mesh. A detailed painted storefront renders via CookedProp.tsx which ships each painted mesh a 512x512=1MB inline texture, so the frame re-hashed tens of MB on the CPU once the storefront was in view; the 16-slot FIFO cache compounded it by thrashing (re-create + re-upload 1MB textures every frame past 16 distinct atlases). This is why a small addition tanked the whole world: the per-frame cost flipped, independent of the 9515 existing meshes. Fix (committed 270173ff5): added a direct-mapped per-frame hash memo keyed by (ptr,len,fingerprint) so a stable buffer is hashed once not per frame (correct under pointer reuse via a cheap fingerprint; never worse than before), grew the cache 16->256 with LRU touch-on-hit, and clear the memo on resetForReload. Built clean via SHIP_RUN_PACKAGE=0 rjit ship hmsc-int. Awaiting live confirmation: restart the dev host and watch the [hb] line — gpu should fall from ~277ms to single-digit ms.
